{ "url": "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/thodel/agentic_historian/607a10015429d53934036f18ebaab772329adb2e/README.md", "checked_at": "2026-11-09T12:22:20Z", "http_status": 200, "content": "# Agentic Historian An agentic pipeline for working with handwritten historical sources — Swiss and German administrative material, 14th to 19th century. It reads a scan, describes the source in codicological terms, extracts and links the persons and places it names, and publishes the result as a reviewable diff on a public site. It **runs no models of its own.** Recognition happens on a serving box, training on a second one, general-purpose LLM work on the institute's GPUStack. This repository is the historian-facing side: the agents, the orchestration, the human-in-the-loop gates, the interface, and the clients that talk to those services. What that separation costs and buys is the subject of half this file. Detailed module documentation lives in [`agentic_historian/README.md`](agentic_historian/README.md); operational runbooks in [`docs/`](docs). --- ## How it was conceived **Agents are roles, not a hierarchy.** The work a historian does with an unknown scan decomposes into things that can be asked separately: read it (A), describe it (B), identify who and where it names (C), situate it in a corpus (D), account for what it cost (E). Each is a module under `agentic_historian/agents/`, each is callable on its own, and `agent_tools.py` exposes all of them under one registry so a planner — or a person — can pick. `orchestrator.py` is wiring, not intelligence; the LLM planner (`nl_orchestrator.py`) is an overlay that can be switched off. **The interface is a chat the seminar already uses.** `bot.py` is a Discord bot and deliberately a thin shell: every command is a few lines over a core module that has no idea Discord exists (`ingest.py`, `orchestrator.py`, `atr_batch.py`). That is what makes the same operations reachable from a cron job, a CLI (`python -m agentic_historian`) and an MCP server without a second implementation. **Two passes, because the first one cannot know what it is reading.** Model selection needs a language, a script and a century; a scan arrives with none of them. So pass 1 reads blind, Agent B describes the source along the Ad-Fontes 16-element framework, and pass 2 reads it again with the models that description implies. A declared language is kept as a *set* — a cartulary with German front matter and Latin charters is both, and the page is only the unit the pipeline happens to have, not a claim that a page has one language. **The human is a gate, not a reviewer at the end.** Gate 1 corrects inferred metadata and re-routes recognition; Gate 2 asks which of several readings is closest; `runstate.py` invalidates exactly the stages a decision affects, so a correction re-runs what it changed and nothing else. **No ground truth is claimed anywhere.** When engines disagree badly the candidates are selected, not merged — a vote over genuinely different readings returns noise. A Gate-2 choice is the closest available reading, bounded by the pool we produced, so the preference log stores *comparisons* (`chosen ≻ offered`) and never transcription text. Everything measured from it — coverage, selection agreement, `regret_cer`, Bradley–Terry engine strength — is a statement about our own selector and our own pool, and a bucket below ~10 comparisons reports *insufficient data* rather than a confident-looking number. The reasoning is in [*Quality without ground truth*](agentic_historian/README.md#quality-without-ground-truth). **Publishing is a commit.** Every processed document goes to [thodel/agentic-historian-outputs](https://github.com/thodel/agentic-historian-outputs) as one atomic commit — transcription, description, entities, `pipeline.json`, rendered page — so a re-run is a diff a historian can read. This repo is a client of it and nothing more: - **One client, one key.** `agent_a/kraken_client.py` speaks `GET /health`, `GET /models`, `POST /segment`, `/recognize`, `/ocr`, authenticated with a static `X-API-Key` (`ATR_GATEWAY_URL`, `ATR_API_KEY`). - **The registry is theirs.** `config/models.yaml` in the serving repo is authoritative. At startup `refresh_kraken_registry()` fetches the live `/models` so `agent_a/model_selector.py` routes language/script/century against what is actually served; the table in `agent_a/models.py` is only a fallback for an unreachable gateway. Registering a model there is enough — no change here. - **Timeouts must respect the other side's budget.** `ATR_HTTP_TIMEOUT` defaults to 300 s because the gateway's own engine budget is 300 s. A tighter client timeout records a phantom failure for an engine that was still working; that is exactly what happened to `trocr-medieval-escriptmask` on 2026-07-16. - **Page-level and line-level are different contracts.** VLM, kraken and party take a page; the TrOCR models need pre-segmented line images, so a page goes through `blla` segmentation first. The ensemble (`agent_a/ensemble.py`, `dual_pipeline.py`) hides the difference from the agents but not from the report. - **Batch runs iterate model-major.** `atr_batch.py` reads every page with one model before moving to the next, because the gateway's VLMs are `residency: lazy` on a single card: page-major would pay an evict-and-reload cycle per page. The run is resumable — the output on disk *is* the state — and it classifies failures rather than catching them (a 404 abandons that model, a timeout is retried, a bad page is stepped over). Runbook: [`docs/BATCH_ATR.md`](docs/BATCH_ATR.md). - **No ranking comes out of it.** A batch answers "how do these models read this collection", not "which is best" — there is no reference text in a run like that. ## Talking to the training service Training moved to [`training-atr-models`](https://github.com/thodel/training-atr-models) on asteraix on 16.09.2026. **This repository trains nothing.** It requests, watches and reports — and it does so through the *same* gateway on idhefix, which proxies `/train/*` to the trainer on `:8204`. There is no second host, no second port and no firewall exception on this path. - **Typed client.** `agent_a/training_client.py` mirrors the recognition client: `POST /train/jobs`, `GET /train/jobs[/{id}]`, `/cancel`, `/log?stage=…`, same key, same lifecycle, job states `queued → preparing → compiling → training → testing → registering → completed|failed|cancelled`. The authority for those words is the trainer's own `contracts.py`, and reading it mattered: this said `done`, which the trainer never sends, so a finished run parsed as `queued` — "still waiting for a card" for a run that was over (#363). - **Today's bot surface is read-only.** `/atr_jobs`, `/atr_job`, `/atr_gpu`, `/atr_progress` (`atr_status.py`) report both machines and label them for what they are: `GET /gpu` is idhefix's cards — the ones recognition runs on — and `GET /train/gpu` is asteraix's, with jobs attributed. Cancelling a job or killing a process from a chat box deserves its own confirm flow and its own decision about who may, so it is not here yet. - **Events, not questions.** `atr_watch.py` announces a run that failed and GPU memory nothing accounts for, once each, because the cases that motivated it were found late by hand: an 11 h run that died unnoticed, and a data-loader worker holding 27,530 MiB for sixteen hours while both cards read 0 % utilisation. It is silent on first sight after a restart, so a deploy never pastes the job history into a channel. - **Starting a run goes through a named preset and a click.** `/train_start` (`training_presets.py`) resolves a preset into the complete request body, shows what it costs and submits only on confirmation; it is admin-gated, and the confirmation is a persistent view with a record on disk, so a restart in between does not kill it (#362, #614). - **A finished run gets a page, with every number labelled.** `/train_publish` and the watcher commit `docs/training//` to the outputs repo: the raw `training.json` and job record, plus a page that gives each measurement its scope, its unit and which way is good. A kraken run carries four numbers that all look like accuracy — the benchmark CER, the `ketos test` CER on line crops from the ground-truth segmentation, kraken's own `val_metric` (an accuracy, pointing the other way, over the ten best checkpoints only) and the eval-harness CER, which this record does **not** have and which therefore prints as not measured rather than letting the `ketos test` number stand in for it (#638). - **Reading and stopping a run.** `/train_log` gives the tail of one stage's log — cut at the front, marked, in a code block, because a traceback is at the end — and answers a missing log by naming the stages the job actually reached. `/train_cancel` is admin-gated with a confirmation and reports what the record says rather than assuming: the trainer signals the process group, the runner writes the terminal state, and the watcher announces it (#364). - **A started run is watched until it ends.** `train_watch.py` keeps one message per run current — stage trail, `queued_reason` verbatim, CER/WER and the log tail at the end — and its registry is on **disk**: a six-hour job cannot sit in the bot's single FIFO queue or inside Discord's 15-minute interaction window, and `/update` restarts this bot by design, so a restart must reattach rather than forget. `/train_status` adopts a run nobody is watching (one started from the API, or before a restart that lost its board); `/train_list` shows the recent ones. Unlike `atr_watch` it is **not** silent on first sight: every run in its registry was put there on purpose, so a run that finished while the bot was down is reported on the next poll (#363). The remaining milestones are in [`docs/TRAINING_INTEGRATION_PLAN.md`](docs/TRAINING_INTEGRATION_PLAN.md). - **Shared state is safe for parallel workers.** One serial worker made plain file I/O safe; R2's workers made it a lottery. `shared_lock.py` now has the piece it was missing: `locked_json`, one lock held across a read, a change and an atomic write. Without it `mark_processed` read the order list, added one id and wrote the whole thing back — two workers finishing two orders each kept their own and erased the other's, so the lost order was re-ingested on the next pull. Measured on the regression: with the old code **12 of 120** ids survived. The knowledge hub was worse, caching the file at construction and rewriting it from that snapshot, so two processes raced for as long as their objects lived (#393). - **Seven questions, not an endpoint.** The corpus graph and the Bestandsgraph (Dodis, Königsfelden, SSRQ, Musiklexikon der Schweiz) are reachable as named queries — persons in care-related documents of a century, every reading of a page with its model and the historian's choice, which authority source links the most and which documents stay unlinked, who is named alongside whom; and, over the Bestandsgraph, who is named in which century across the four holdings with role and authority id, who signs with whom (Dodis), and which families have which members and places (KF, SSRQ). One mention path, `(P128/P67)|P67`, serves both graphs. `/sparql` runs them; `knowledge_hub/queries.py` holds them. Every row carries the document it came from, enforced in the constructor rather than by review, and no caller's text ever becomes query syntax ([`docs/KG_QUERIES.md`](docs/KG_QUERIES.md), #331, #654). - **The loop closes through the registry, not through this repo.** A finished run registers on the shared research share; the serving gateway picks the registration up and advertises the model at `/models`; the next `refresh_kraken_registry()` makes it selectable here. A model trained on Monday is routable on Tuesday without a commit in this repository. - **Two CER numbers that must not be confused.** `ketos test` CER (line crops from ground-truth segmentation) and eval-harness CER (a full page through our own segmentation) measure different things and will disagree. Any report that carries a number must say which, against which reference, under which normalisation. ## The other services - **GPUStack** (`gpustack.unibe.ch/v1`, OpenAI-compatible) serves the general-purpose models by role: vision `qwen3.8-27b` for Agents A/B, text `gpt-oss-120b` for C/D/E, `minimax-m2.7` reserved for orchestration. Routing is in `config.py`; `gpt-oss-120b` is a reasoning model, so text calls need a generous `max_tokens` floor. No Claude, no Gemini — everything stays in-house. - **MCP federation** on tei (`/mcp/kf`, `/mcp/ssrq`, `/mcp/hls`, `/mcp/hbls`, `/mcp/eos`) supplies authority data for Agent C's entity linking, queried in parallel and merged by `utils/entity_resolver.py`. The registry is declarative (`knowledge_hub/mcp_registry.py`); a new source is a reviewed PR, never a hot-load. - **`mcp_atr/`** is the inverse direction: a small MCP server on tei that lets an agent session *drive* this stack — mirror a share, start a batch, poll it, read what it produced. It exists because a cloud session cannot open a socket to tei at all, while MCP is dialled by the broker over 443. It is a door of exactly eight tools, never a shell: a caller chooses which corpus and which models and can never choose a command, a flag or a path outside the corpus roots. ([`deploy/mcp-atr/`](deploy/mcp-atr), [`docs/CLAUDE_CODE_CONNECTIVITY.md`](docs/CLAUDE_CODE_CONNECTIVITY.md)) - **Voyant** at `tei.dh.unibe.ch/voyant/` backs Agent D's corpus views. - **A corpus analysis says how much of the corpus it saw.** Agent D cuts a long corpus into overlapping chunks and asks the model per chunk; a chunk that does not answer now shows up as a `provenance` block — how many chunks there were, how many answered, and the character range of each gap — instead of contributing an empty list that reads as "nothing found" (#634). `complete: true` with an empty list therefore means *measured, nothing there*. The three analyses also appear in `report.md`, which named only words and characters before and so hid both the results and their gaps. - **Nextcloud / SwitchDrive** shares are the ingestion side: a folder of scans is mirrored, or read straight over WebDAV with a page cache in front of it. --- ## Layout | path | | |---|---| | `agentic_historian/` | the package — agents, orchestrator, gates, clients, bot, MCP server ([its README](agentic_historian/README.md) documents every module) | | `docs/` | runbooks and plans: batch ATR, training integration, evaluation harness, connectivity, Nextcloud, lessons; literature comparisons ([SPIRE](docs/SPIRE_COMPARISON.md)) with citation files in `docs/references/` | | `deploy/` | systemd units and nginx config for the pieces that run on tei, and the environment template (`gpustack.env.example`) | ## Running it Python 3.11 or 3.12, on the unibe VPN. From the repository root: ```bash python3.12 -m venv .venv .venv/bin/python -m pip install -r requirements-dev.txt .venv/bin/python -m pip install -e agentic_historian --no-deps --no-build-isolation .venv/bin/python -m ruff check agentic_historian .venv/bin/python -m pytest agentic_historian/tests ``` The suite is offline: GPUStack, the ATR gateway, MCP, WebDAV, Voyant, Discord and GitHub are mocked at their boundaries, and CI runs it on every PR. Configuration for development is a single `.env.gpustack` at the repository root (gitignored; template in `deploy/gpustack.env.example`) — every variable is listed in [`agentic_historian/README.md`](agentic_historian/README.md#environment-variables-envgpustack-repo-root). In production the bot runs on tei under `agentic-historian.service` as its own user, and since 23.10.2026 it reads **only** `/etc/agentic_historian.env` (`AH_ENV_FILE`); the dotenv files in the checkout are the CLI's — [`docs/DEPLOYMENT_TEI.md`](docs/DEPLOYMENT_TEI.md) says what a deploy does now. What this bot does and what `dh-bot` (the Hermes agent on the same server) does — one table, one rule, every slash command — is [`docs/BOTS.md`](docs/BOTS.md). As a **standalone** process (separation epic #565) it is decoupled from the `dh-bot` agent (OpenClaw until 06.11.2026, Hermes since — [`docs/BOTS.md`](docs/BOTS.md)): its own Discord token, its own secrets file (`deploy/systemd/agentic_historian.env.example` → `/etc/agentic_historian.env`, read via `AH_ENV_FILE`) separate from the shared `.env.gpustack`, a hardened systemd unit, the LLM-orchestration overlay off by default, and the agent's former home (`workspace/`) no longer in this repository (S3, #568) — see [`deploy/systemd/SEPARATION.md`](deploy/systemd/SEPARATION.md). S2 (own secrets, sandbox, own user) is in force on tei since 23.10.2026 and measured by `deploy/systemd/check_separation.py`; the bot's own Discord application (S1, #566) since 04.11.2026; the key rotation (S2 item 4) is #802. CI's `standalone` job proves the bot builds and starts without any agent workspace. Contribution rules — one issue, one branch off `origin/main`, one PR, never stacked — are in [`agentic_historian/README.md`](agentic_historian/README.md#contributing--pr--issue-rules), and they are there because each of them has been violated at least once. GED Merge

A complete GEDCOM editor that runs entirely in your browser.
Edit your family tree, merge a second file into it field by field, and keep the whole file healthy.

--- Genealogy programs export GEDCOM, but they merge it badly: import a cousin's file and you get duplicate people, two spellings of every village, and dates in a format your file has never used. GED Merge does the opposite — it reshapes the incoming file into *your* file's conventions, scores every candidate pair, and then shows you both sides of every field so **you** decide what survives. Nothing is uploaded, and nothing changes until you say so. - **Live app:** — no account, no install, works offline once loaded - **User's Guide:** · Slovenščina: - **Changelog:** · Slovenščina: - **Privacy:** · **Terms:** > This README is for **developers**. For how to *use* the app, read the User's Guide above. ## What it looks like **Merge** — the scored candidate list, and one row per field with the main file on the left, the incoming file on the right, and a Main / Incoming / Both choice wherever they disagree: ![Merge mode: candidate list and field-by-field comparison](docs/screenshots/merge.png) **Edit** — a full editor for the loaded file: names, events, families, notes, sources and media: ![Edit mode: a person with their parents, events and notes](docs/screenshots/edit.png) **Charts** — tree, grid, fan, circle, timeline, relationship path, map and printable reports: ![Fan chart of an ancestry](docs/screenshots/chart.png) ## Features **Edit** — every record in the file: names and alternate names, events and attributes, families and relationships, notes, sources and citations, media with crop tagging, and privacy flags. Unified undo/redo across edits and merge decisions. **Merge** — load a second GEDCOM (or a [indeks.rodoslovje.si](https://indeks.rodoslovje.si) matches CSV), get scored candidate pairs ranked by kinship distance from a start person, and resolve each one field by field. The incoming file is normalized to your file's house style first — date format, place layout, link languages, GEDCOM version — so you are comparing like with like. Saving produces a merged file plus a human-readable change report. **Tools** — whole-file maintenance: a health check, a within-file duplicate finder with clustering, bulk normalization, a privacy redactor, and source and place browsers with geocoding. **Charts, maps and reports** — eight views of the same tree, all exportable (SVG, PNG, PDF, and PDF split across several sheets for a wall-sized chart), plus Ahnentafel and NGSQ register reports in list or narrative form. **Faithful to your file** — the parser keeps a lossless line tree, so tags GED Merge does not understand still round-trip unchanged. Vendor tags from the major programs are recognized rather than discarded. **Bilingual** — the entire interface, guide and changelog exist in English and Slovenian. ## Privacy Your GEDCOM file is never uploaded: parsing, matching, merging, editing, the charts and every tool run on your own device, and the site has no upload endpoint and no API. Two features make network requests, both **off by default** and both switched on by you: - **Online lookups** — a place name, a house number or a source URL sent to OpenStreetMap, the GURS registers, GOV, or a public CORS relay. - **Base-map tiles** — the map background, which tells the tile provider roughly where you are looking. Off, maps draw on a bundled offline world outline. There is no account, no analytics, no third-party script and no tracking cookie; the fonts are self-hosted. The [Privacy Policy](https://gedmerge.com/privacy/) names every provider, says what is sent, and lists what the app stores in your browser. ## Getting started Prerequisites: **Node.js 24** or newer (the version CI uses is in [`.nvmrc`](.nvmrc); npm ships with it). ```bash npm install # install dependencies npm run dev # start the Vite dev server, then open the printed localhost URL ``` There is nothing else to configure — no environment variables, no services, no database. Drop one of the files in [`public/samples/`](public/samples) (royal families, US presidents) onto the landing page to try it without your own data. ## Scripts | Command | What it does | |---------|--------------| | `npm run dev` | Start the Vite dev server. | | `npm run build` | Type-check (`tsc -b`) **and** produce the production bundle in `dist/`. | | `npm run preview` | Serve the built `dist/` locally. | | `npm run typecheck` | `tsc -b --noEmit`. Note: incremental build caching can make this a no-op — prefer `npm run build` (or `tsc -b --force`) for a guaranteed full type-check. | | `npm run lint` | ESLint with `--max-warnings 0`. | | `npm run test` | Run the Vitest unit tests once. | | `npm run test:watch` | Vitest in watch mode. | | `npm run test:coverage` | Unit tests with the per-directory coverage floors CI enforces. | | `npm run test:e2e` | Run the Playwright end-to-end tests. | Run a single unit test file: ```bash npx vitest run src/gedcom/date.test.ts ``` ## Architecture A browser-only React app. All data stays local. - **Data model** (`src/gedcom/types.ts`) — two layers: a lossless raw line tree (`GedNode`, level/tag/value/children, so nothing is dropped on save) and a typed domain model (`Individual`, `Family`, `Dataset`) projected on top for matching and the UI. - **Web Worker** (`src/worker/`) — owns the parse → normalize → match pipeline off the main thread, communicating via typed messages. - **Normalize** (`src/normalize/`) — reshapes an incoming file to the main file's date/place/link "house style" before comparison. - **Match** (`src/match/`) — scores candidate pairs 0–100 over weighted fields, and ranks them by kinship distance from a chosen home person. - **Merge** (`src/merge/`) — applies per-field decisions to produce a merged `GedNode[]` plus a change report. - **Tools** (`src/tools/`) — whole-file maintenance (validation, duplicate finder, bulk normalize, sources, places) as pure functions. - **Chart / report / geo** (`src/chart/`, `src/report/`, `src/geo/`) — pure layout, text and gazetteer logic with no React in it. - **UI** (`src/ui/`) — React components. App state lives in `src/App.tsx`. The build is **multi-page**: the app (`index.html`) plus the static, crawlable guide, changelog and legal pages (`guide/`, `navodila/`, `changelog/`, `posodobitve/`, `privacy/`, `zasebnost/`, `terms/`, `pogoji/`). **Browser support:** any current browser. Chrome and Edge additionally get the File System Access API features — a remembered media folder and reopening the file you loaded — where Firefox and Safari use an in-memory fallback. ### Further reading | Document | What's in it | |----------|--------------| | [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) | Module map and development workflow; the detailed rules (architecture and CSS conventions, GEDCOM compliance, Slovenian copy, merging) are in [docs/agents/](docs/agents/). | | [MATCHING.md](MATCHING.md) | The matching algorithm: pipeline stages, weights, gates, penalties, calibrated thresholds, and how to verify a change to any of them. | | [MAPVIEW.md](MAPVIEW.md) | Map and geocoding design — providers, caching, the coordinate write-back. | | [IDEAS.md](IDEAS.md) | The backlog: what might come next, and what was deliberately rejected. | ## Contributing Issues and pull requests are welcome — bug reports especially, since GEDCOM files in the wild vary far more than any test corpus. A GEDCOM snippet that reproduces the problem is worth more than a description, but please **redact it first** (the app's Tools › Privacy does this) — do not attach a file containing living people. Before opening a PR: ```bash npm run build && npm run lint && npm run test && npm run test:e2e ``` CI runs lint, typecheck, the unit suite with coverage floors, and the Playwright suite on every pull request. All changes reach `main` through a pull request: direct pushes are refused, and a PR merges (with a merge commit) only once CI is green. Two house rules worth knowing: user-facing strings change in **both** `src/locales/en.ts` and `src/locales/sl.ts` in the same commit, and colours and radii come from the design tokens in `src/theme/heritage-pine.css` rather than literals. `AGENTS.md` and `docs/agents/` have the rest. Regenerate the screenshots above after a UI change with `node scripts/screenshots.mjs` (with the dev server running). ## Data sources and credits The optional online features build on public services, each under its own terms: OpenStreetMap and Nominatim, Overpass, GeoNames, the [GOV](https://gov.genealogy.net/) genealogical gazetteer, Slovenia's [GURS](https://www.e-prostor.gov.si/) registers and map services, and the CARTO, OpenTopoMap, Esri, swisstopo and IGN France tile services. Historical map overlays come from the David Rumsey Map Collection and national mapping agencies. Typeset in IBM Plex. ## License [MIT](LICENSE.md) © Luka Renko. You may use, modify and redistribute the code, including commercially. The GED Merge name and logo are not covered by that grant — see the [Terms](https://gedmerge.com/terms/). ## Build & deploy ```bash npm run build # → dist/ : a self-contained static site ``` `dist/` can be hosted on any static file server (the live site runs on Caddy behind Cloudflare; GitHub Pages, Netlify or Vercel work equally well). The app is an installable PWA and works offline after the first load. Every green push to `main` is deployed to the test site on GitHub Pages ([test.gedmerge.com](https://test.gedmerge.com)), which is kept out of search engines.   "http_status": 200,
  "content": "# geneanet-drift

Folds the edits a relative makes in their Geneanet tree back into your Gramps
Web tree. A browser extension saves the Geneanet pages you open; this tool
compares the saved pages with Gramps, lets you accept, edit or reject each
difference in a local web page, and writes the accepted ones to Gramps.

## What it does and does not do

- The Python tool never contacts Geneanet. Geneanet's terms prohibit automatic
  access. The browser extension (below) acts only on a page you opened
  yourself: it never requests, navigates, clicks, scrolls or paginates. It
  saves the DOM your browser already rendered, the same as select-all and copy,
  and saves an image only when you click for it, like "Save image as". That is
  the author's reading, not legal advice; Geneanet may still treat any
  page-reading extension as a tool.
- Reading Gramps is GET-only. Give the read user no write permissions but
  `ViewPrivate`; it refuses a user that cannot view private records, because
  the snapshot would silently omit those people. Only `geneanet-drift apply` and
  `undo` write, as a separate Editor user that must hold `AddObject` and
  `EditObject` and nothing beyond the Editor role.
- Nothing is written without a dry-run preview, a typed confirmation and a
  Gramps XML backup taken first.

Links between his people and yours are stored in Gramps itself: a Citation
under the Source `Geneanet - <tree> family tree` whose `page` is his display name
for the person. The private data directory holds `decisions.json`,
`applied.json`, `backups/` and an optional hand-written `negatives.json` of
rejected pairings.

## Install

`uv tool install .` or `pip install .`; everything below is identical either way.

## Browser extension

`extension/` saves the Geneanet tree pages you open (person pages, the list of
all individuals and the data entry history) to
`Downloads/geneanet-drift/<tree>/pages/`, so you can reconcile a whole tree
without exporting it. It works in Chrome and Firefox from one manifest and has
no build step.

- Chrome: open `chrome://extensions`, enable Developer mode, choose Load
  unpacked and select `extension/`.
- Firefox: open `about:debugging#/runtime/this-firefox` and choose Load
  Temporary Add-on, then select `extension/manifest.json`. The add-on is
  removed when Firefox restarts; the saved pages are not.

Open the extension's Options, enter the tree name, and on Firefox choose Grant
access. Then browse: each person page you open is saved, and the popup lists
the people you have not opened yet. Pages are only saved while a tree name is
set. Edit forms are never saved. The data entry history page is saved as
`history-editing.html` beside the person pages.

## Configure

The tool remembers everything it can and prompts only for what it deliberately
refuses to remember: the Gramps passwords.

The data directory holds `config.toml`, `.env` and the tool's state. Point
`--data-dir` or `GENEANET_DRIFT_DATA` at it (default
`$XDG_DATA_HOME/geneanet-drift`), then copy `config.example.toml` there as
`config.toml`.

`tree` is the slug in your relative's Geneanet URL with the `_w` suffix removed:
`https://gw.geneanet.org/example_w` is `tree = "example"`.

| setting | environment | `.env` | `config.toml` | prompt |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| data directory | `GENEANET_DRIFT_DATA` | no | no | no |
| `tree` | no | no | `tree` | no |
| Gramps URL | `GRAMPS_URL` | yes | `gramps_url` | no |
| Gramps user | `GRAMPS_USER` | yes | `gramps_user` | no |
| Gramps password | `GRAMPS_PASSWORD` | yes | never | yes |
| Gramps write user (Editor role, `apply` and `undo` only) | `GRAMPS_WRITE_USER` | yes | `gramps_write_user` | no |
| Gramps write password | `GRAMPS_WRITE_PASSWORD` | yes | never | yes |

Within a row, the process environment beats `<data dir>/.env`, which beats
`config.toml`. With no terminal and no password set, the tool exits with an
error instead of prompting. The write rows are read only by `apply` and `undo`.

```sh
echo 'GRAMPS_PASSWORD=...' > <data dir>/.env && chmod 600 <data dir>/.env
```

`.env` cannot set `GENEANET_DRIFT_DATA`, because it is found inside the data
directory. Its format is `KEY=VALUE` lines, `#` comments, an optional `export `
prefix and optional surrounding quotes; there is no interpolation, escape
sequences or multi-line values.

## Workflow

Run these in order. `DIR` is the capture folder, by default
`~/Downloads/geneanet-drift/<tree>/pages`.

1. Capture. `geneanet-drift` (the same as `geneanet-drift capture-status`) reads
   the saved change log `DIR/history-editing.html` and lists every person in it
   whose captured page is missing or older than their newest change (file time
   against the change time), each with the address to open. No sync state is
   kept: capturing a page is what clears it from the list. Geneanet's times are
   compared as written against your local file times, so a change within a few
   hours of a capture may need a manual check. Open those pages with the
   extension on, rerun to check, and repeat until nothing is left. Options:
   `--pages DIR`, `--since YYYY-MM-DD` to list only changes from that date on,
   and `--feed FILE` to read a pasted copy of the change log (the page in
   English, select-all, paste into a plain-text file) instead of the saved
   page.
2. Snapshot. `geneanet-drift snapshot --out FILE` saves the Gramps tree (read
   user) to a JSON file outside this repository.
3. Review. `geneanet-drift review --pages DIR --snapshot FILE [--port N]` serves
   the review page on `127.0.0.1` (default: a free port) and prints its URL.
   Accept, edit or reject each change, and choose the matching Gramps person
   where names are ambiguous. Decisions are saved to `decisions.json`, so a
   review can span sittings. Photos show only when their originals were saved
   next to `DIR` (`../media/person-<n>/`).
4. Apply. `geneanet-drift apply --pages DIR` builds a plan from the accepted
   decisions, prints it (the dry run is always shown), and writes it only after
   you type the confirmation. Before any write it saves a Gramps XML backup to
   `<data dir>/backups/` through the read user and stops if that fails. Each
   write is logged to `<data dir>/applied.json` with its created and updated
   objects and transaction ids; a rerun skips logged steps and stops, without
   writing, if a logged object has since changed.
   `geneanet-drift undo --last N` reverts the newest N logged steps, newest
   first.
5. GEDCOM, optionally. `geneanet-drift gedcom --pages DIR --out FILE` exports
   the captured person pages (`DIR` holds `person-<n>.html`) as GEDCOM 5.5.1.
   Media `FILE` paths are relative to the capture folder of the tree
   (`media/person-<n>/...`).

Keep the data directory in its own private repository, and list `.env` in that
repository's `.gitignore`. The tool refuses to run if the data
directory is inside its own git work tree.

## Keeping personal data out of this repository

gitleaks in CI catches credentials, not names. Personal data stays out by
structure: test fixtures use invented names only, the data directory is
outside the repository, and `.gitignore` lists the files the
tool writes.

## Contributing

`uv run --extra dev pytest` and `uv run --extra dev ruff check .`. For the
extension, `node --test "tests/extension/*.test.js"` and
`npx --yes addons-linter@10.14.0 extension`.

release continues the work on the map: places can now bring their own **map files**, so the boundaries of a parish or a route in KML, GeoJSON or GPX appear right on the map, **Wikidata buildings** can be saved to your tree with one click, and all map labels are now shown **in your language**. Beyond the map, the object lists get an **advanced filter** that combines any of the Gramps filter rules, admins can **create and restore backups** directly in the app, and you can **link several sign-in methods** to your account. Three new contributors joined with a long list of bug fixes. Welcome! :rocket:\\r\\n\\r\\nSeveral of the new features rely on new endpoints in [Gramps Web API v3.24](https://github.com/gramps-project/gramps-web-api/releases/tag/v3.24.0), the server component included in the release images. They degrade gracefully on older backend versions.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Map View\\r\\n\\r\\n### Map files of places\\r\\n\\r\\nWhen you select a place on the map, the **KML, GeoJSON and GPX files** attached to it as media objects are drawn on the map, e.g. the boundaries of a parish or a route. This also works for places without coordinates. While a place is selected, its files are listed in the layer switcher under \\\"Your maps\\\" and can be switched off there.\\r\\n\\r\\nImplemented in #1524, #1552\\r\\n\\r\\n### Save Wikidata buildings as places\\r\\n\\r\\nThe details of a Wikidata building have a new **Save as place** button, which opens the new place form prefilled with the building's name, type, coordinates and a link to Wikidata. If the building is already in your tree, the button opens the existing place. This lets you use the historical buildings collected in [Domus](https://domus.genealogy.net/) in your own tree.\\r\\n\\r\\nImplemented in #1528\\r\\n\\r\\n### Labels in your language\\r\\n\\r\\nThe labels of the base map and the historical map are now shown **in the language you selected in Gramps Web**, for all its languages, and fall back to the local name. Closes #1460.\\r\\n\\r\\nImplemented in #1521, #1522\\r\\n\\r\\n## Advanced Filter\\r\\n\\r\\nThe filter panel of the object lists has a new **Advanced filter** button, which opens a condition builder for everything the filter facets can't express. Conditions are the filter rules known from Gramps desktop, picked from a searchable list. They can be combined in groups with *All conditions*, *Any condition* or *Exactly one condition*, and groups and conditions can be nested and negated. Each parameter gets a matching input, e.g. a date field, a tag selector or the object selector for IDs.\\r\\n\\r\\nActive facet filters open in the builder as conditions, and a simple filter goes back to the facet pills when you're done. The rules are shown in your language with Gramps Web API v3.24.\\r\\n\\r\\nImplemented in #1506\\r\\n\\r\\n## Backups\\r\\n\\r\\nThe admin settings have a new **Backups** section. You can **create, download and delete backups** stored on the server, and **restore** from a stored backup or an uploaded file. Before restoring, you choose what to restore (data, tree settings and users) and get a preview of the changes. The restore from a Gramps XML file moved into the same upload, so the Danger Zone now only contains \\\"Delete all objects\\\". Managing backups needs a new permission and Gramps Web API v3.24.\\r\\n\\r\\nImplemented in #1544\\r\\n\\r\\n## Linked Sign-in Methods\\r\\n\\r\\nIf your server uses single sign-on (OIDC), you can now **link and unlink sign-in methods** under Settings > Account, e.g. to sign in to an existing account with Google or Microsoft. Part of #770, implemented by @scotCW in https://github.com/gramps-project/gramps-web/pull/1547\\r\\n\\r\\n## Other New Features\\r\\n\\r\\n* In edit mode, a person without media shows a profile picture placeholder with a menu to upload or select a media object, and the first image in the gallery is marked as the profile picture. Closes #1414. Implemented by @lukasganster in https://github.com/gramps-project/gramps-web/pull/1525\\r\\n* When another task is already running on the tree, e.g. an import or a reindex, starting a new one now shows a clear message and the running task with its progress. Finished tasks in the notification log read \\\"Task completed\\\" or \\\"Task failed\\\", and clicking a failed task shows its error. #1535\\r\\n* When the limit for media archive exports is reached, the error message now shows the configured limit. #1534\\r\\n* The first-run wizard no longer asks for the e-mail settings, which are set in the server configuration.
